python3 scripts/goal_guard.py --arm .goal/planning-sweep.json
Jon's goal, verbatim: 'address everything in docs/planning and every follow
up that is found while implementing docs planning. The hook should basically
say: there's no way you finished everything in docs/planning, get back to it.'
So this goal is DELIBERATELY not closeable by finishing a fixed list. The
ledger check below reads docs/planning/queue-24h-2026-07-26.md, and the rule
written at the top of that file is: if every row is closed, go find the next
thing in docs/planning and add it. An empty queue is a signal to refill it.
Check design notes:
* The ledger marker check is the OPEN-ENDED half, and the guard's own
docstring is right that a doc marker is a file I can edit. That is why
every named finding ALSO has a hard check beside it: a named test that
must pass, or a code path that must be gone. Editing the ledger alone
cannot release this run.
* Every check was verified RED at arming. A guard that is green at minute
zero guards nothing (learned 2026-07-26: check 7.1c passed on day zero
because it named symbols that did not exist).
* $HOME/.cargo/bin/cargo everywhere: the hook PATH has no cargo, and a
'command not found' compile check can NEVER pass, wedging the run.
* Test checks assert a POSITIVE pass count. A cargo test filter that
matches zero tests EXITS 0, so naming an unwritten test would otherwise
pass before the work is done.
* SIGPIPE footgun (hit 2026-07-26): `cmd | grep -q pat` is NONDETERMINISTIC
here. grep -q exits on first match, the writer gets SIGPIPE, and the
guard sets pipefail -- so the check reports 141/101 whenever grep wins
the race. Never end a pipeline with grep -q; use plain grep >/dev/null.
* Full ./run_tests.sh is pre-commit discipline, NOT a guard check: it does
not fit the hook timeout, and a check that cannot finish cannot close.

Check-authoring lesson, 2026-07-26: the first A7/A8 checks grepped for the ABSENCE of text (`With<FeatureSimEntity>`, `Update,`) and both went red on PROSE -- the phrase appeared in a docstring explaining the fix, and `Update,` is still correct for the asset-load systems in the same file. An absence-of-a-string check fails the moment anyone documents the thing. Name a TEST that asserts the property instead.

A11 recurrence, THIRD time: an absence-of-string check went red on prose again -- this time `CharacterLoadDemand` inside the docstring that explains why registration no longer calls it. The rule is now absolute: NEVER grep for the absence of an identifier. Name a test. Documenting a removal must not break the guard that verified it.
goal: address everything in docs/planning, and every follow-up found while implementing it. There is no way this is finished -- if the queue in docs/planning/queue-24h-2026-07-26.md looks empty, that means the next item has not been WRITTEN DOWN yet, not that the work is done. Go read docs/planning, find it, add it, and get back to it.
